questions.question: Which of the following is a ring compound with the molecular formula C₆H₁₂?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclohexane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclohexane** is an **alicyclic hydrocarbon** belonging to the **cycloalkane** series, characterized by a closed-ring structure.
 
• The molecular formula **C₆H₁₂** follows the general formula for cycloalkanes, which is **CₙH₂ₙ**.
 
• Each of the six carbon atoms in the ring is **sp³ hybridized**, forming **sigma bonds** with two adjacent carbon atoms and two hydrogen atoms.
 
• Because all carbon-carbon bonds are **single bonds**, cyclohexane is classified as a **saturated hydrocarbon**.
 
• To maintain the tetrahedral bond angle of approximately 109.5 degrees and minimize **ring strain**, it adopts non-planar conformations, the most stable being the **chair conformation**.
 
• It is widely used in the industrial production of **nylon** precursors like **adipic acid** and **caprolactam**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Benzene**:

 
 
• It is a **cyclic** and **aromatic hydrocarbon** with the molecular formula **C₆H₆**.
 
• It features a **planar hexagonal ring** with a **delocalized pi-electron system** and alternating double bonds.
 
 
 
• **Hexane**:
 
 
• It is an **acyclic** or **straight-chain alkane** with the molecular formula **C₆H₁₄**.
 
• It follows the general formula **CₙH₂ₙ₊₂** and does not contain a ring structure.
 
 
 
• **Butane**:
 
 
• It is an **alkane** with four carbon atoms and the molecular formula **C₄H₁₀**.
 
• It is an **open-chain hydrocarbon** commonly utilized as a component of **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)**.

questions.question: What is the pH of a 0.01 M HCl solution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** is a **strong monoprotic acid**, which means it undergoes **complete dissociation** in an aqueous solution to release **hydrogen ions [H⁺]**.
 
• For a **0.01 M HCl** solution, the concentration of **hydrogen ions** is equal to the concentration of the acid itself, which is **0.01 moles per liter** or **10−² M**.
 
• The **pH scale** was developed by **Søren Sørensen** in **1909** as a way to quantify the **acidity** or **alkalinity** of a substance using a **logarithmic scale**.
 
• The mathematical formula used to calculate the **pH** is **pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]**, where [H⁺] represents the **molar concentration** of hydrogen ions.
 
• By substituting the value, we calculate **pH = −log₁₀(0.01)**. Since **0.01** is **10−²**, the logarithm of **10−²** is **−2**.
 
• The final calculation, **−(−2)**, results in a **pH value of 2**, indicating that the solution is **highly acidic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of the pH Scale**:

 
 
• The **pH scale** typically ranges from **0 to 14** at standard room temperature (**25°C**).
 
• A **pH of 7** is defined as **neutral**, which is the value for **pure water** where the concentration of **H⁺** equals **OH−**.
 
• Values **less than 7** signify **acidity**, while values **greater than 7** signify **basicity** or alkalinity.
 
 
 
• **Concentration and Strength**:
 
 
• **Molarity (M)** is the **unit of concentration** representing the number of **moles of solute** per **liter** of solution.
 
• **Strong acids** like **HCl**, **H₂SO₄**, and **HNO₃** have extremely high **acid dissociation constants (Kₐ)**, unlike **weak acids** like **citric acid**.
 
• The **pH** of human **gastric juice** is approximately **1.5 to 3.5**, which closely aligns with the acidity of a **0.01 M** to **0.1 M** hydrochloric acid solution.

questions.question: How long does an unfertilized egg survive after being released from the ovary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Almost a day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ovulation** is the biological process where a mature **oocyte** (egg) is released from the **Graafian follicle** of the ovary into the **Fallopian tube**.
 
• Once released, the egg remains viable for fertilization for a very limited window, typically lasting between **12 to 24 hours**. This timeframe aligns with the description of **almost a day**.
 
• The egg moves through the **ampulla** of the Fallopian tube, which is the primary site where fertilization by **sperm** occurs.
 
• If the egg is not fertilized within this **24-hour** period, it begins to undergo **apoptosis** (programmed cell death) and loses its metabolic activity.
 
• Following its degradation, the unfertilized egg is eventually absorbed by the body or shed along with the **uterine lining** (endometrium) during the **menstrual phase** of the cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hormonal Triggers**:

 
 
• The release of the egg is triggered by a sharp rise in **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)**, known as the **LH surge**, which occurs approximately 14 days before the start of the next period.
 
• **Estrogen** levels rise before ovulation to prepare the **cervical mucus**, making it more hospitable for sperm survival.
 
 
 
• **Reproductive Longevity**:
 
 
• While the egg survives for only **one day**, human **sperm** can survive inside the female reproductive tract for **3 to 5 days**.
 
• This difference in longevity creates a **fertile window** of about 6 days, during which intercourse can lead to pregnancy even if it occurs several days before ovulation.
 
 
 
• **Post-Ovulation Phase**:
 
 
• After the egg is released, the empty follicle transforms into the **Corpus Luteum**, which secretes **Progesterone** to thicken the **endometrium** for possible implantation.

questions.question: Which group of organisms is responsible for breaking down dead bodies and waste into simple substances, returning them to the soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decomposers** are specialized organisms, predominantly **fungi** and **bacteria**, that perform the vital function of breaking down complex organic matter from **dead remains** and nitrogenous wastes.
 
• They utilize **enzymes** to decompose organic molecules into simpler inorganic forms, such as **carbon dioxide**, **water**, and **nutrients** like **nitrogen** and **phosphorus**.
 
• By returning these essential elements to the **soil**, decomposers ensure **nutrient cycling**, which maintains soil fertility and allows **autotrophs** to thrive.
 
• In the **trophic structure**, they occupy a unique position as they process energy from all levels once the organisms die, effectively acting as the **recycling unit** of the **biosphere**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Producers**:

 
 
• Identified as **autotrophs**, these organisms, including **green plants** and **cyanobacteria**, synthesize their own organic food using sunlight via **photosynthesis**.
 
• They represent the **base** of the **ecological pyramid**.
 
 
 
• **Consumers**:
 
 
• These are **heterotrophs** that cannot manufacture food and must ingest other organisms.
 
• They include **herbivores** (primary), **carnivores** (secondary/tertiary), and **omnivores**.
 
 
 
• **Parasites**:
 
 
• Organisms that sustain themselves by living on or within a **host** organism, often causing **pathogenic** effects or nutritional depletion.
 
• Examples include **Plasmodium**, **leeches**, and **Cuscuta** plants.

questions.question: The SI unit of force (F) is __________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Force (F)** is defined as any interaction that, when unopposed, changes the motion of an object. In physics, the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration is governed by **Newton's Second Law of Motion**.
 
• The mathematical formula for force is **F = m × a**, where **m** represents **mass** and **a** represents **acceleration**.
 
• In the **International System of Units (SI)**, the standard unit for **mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**, and the standard unit for **acceleration** is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• By substituting these base units into the formula, the derived SI unit for force becomes **kg m/s²**.
 
• This specific combination of base units is formally named the **Newton (N)**, where **1 N = 1 kg m/s²**, signifying the force needed to accelerate a **1 kg** mass at **1 m/s²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule**:

 
 
• The SI unit for **Work** and **Energy**.
 
• It is defined as the work done when a force of **one Newton** displaces an object by **one meter**.
 
• Dimensionally, it is represented as **kg m²/s²**.
 
 
 
• **N m (Newton-meter)**:
 
 
• Commonly used as the unit for **Torque** or **Moment of Force**.
 
• While it is dimensionally equivalent to the **Joule**, it is used specifically for rotational force to distinguish it from scalar energy units.
 
 
 
• **kg m/s**:
 
 
• The SI unit for **Linear Momentum (p)** and **Impulse (J)**.
 
• It represents the product of an object's **mass** and its **velocity**.
 
• It describes the quantity of motion possessed by a moving body.

questions.question: If a sample of air is compressed to half its volume, which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The composition of air remains same because it is a mixture.
Air becomes a compound on compression.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The composition of air remains same because it is a mixture.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Air** is a **homogeneous mixture** of various gases, primarily **Nitrogen (78%)**, **Oxygen (21%)**, and trace amounts of **Argon** and **Carbon Dioxide**. Since these components are not **chemically bonded**, they retain their individual properties even when physical conditions change. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• When a sample of air is compressed, the **intermolecular distance** between the gas molecules decreases, but the total number of molecules of each gas type remains constant within the container. Therefore, the **ratio** or **proportion** of the constituent gases does not alter. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Compression** is a purely **physical change** that affects state variables like **pressure**, **volume**, and **density**. It does not involve any **chemical transformation**, meaning the molecular **composition** of the air remains identical before and after compression. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The formation of a **compound** requires a **chemical reaction** involving the breaking and forming of **chemical bonds** in fixed **stoichiometric proportions**. Physical compression does not provide the conditions or the mechanism to turn a gaseous mixture into a compound. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boyle's Law**:

 
 
• This law states that for a fixed amount of an ideal gas kept at a constant **temperature**, **Pressure (P)** is inversely proportional to **Volume (V)**.
 
• The mathematical relationship is expressed as P times V = k . When the volume is reduced to half, the **pressure** of the air sample doubles, but the **chemical identity** of the gas molecules remains the same.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Mixtures**:
 
 
• **Variable Composition**: Unlike compounds, mixtures do not have a fixed formula, though a trapped sample maintains its ratio unless filtered.
 
• **Physical Separation**: Components of air can be separated using physical methods such as **fractional distillation** of liquid air.
 
• **Energy Changes**: No energy (in the form of heat or light) is significantly released or absorbed during the simple mixing or compression of air gases at standard conditions.

questions.question: In the process of electrolytic refining of copper, which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrolyte – Acidified Copper Sulfate Solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the process of **electrolytic refining** of copper, the **electrolyte** consists of a water-soluble salt of the metal, specifically an **acidified copper sulfate solution** (CuSO₄), which allows the transfer of **copper ions**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **anode** is made from a thick block of **impure copper** that is to be purified; during electrolysis, copper atoms from the anode lose electrons and enter the solution as ions. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **cathode** is a thin strip of **pure copper** where the dissolved **Cu²⁺** ions from the electrolyte gain electrons and deposit as high-purity metal. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Anode mud** consists of insoluble impurities like **antimony**, **selenium**, **silver**, and **gold** that settle at the bottom of the cell specifically under the **anode**, not the cathode. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Transformations**:

 
 
• At the **Anode** (Oxidation): Cu (impure) → Cu²⁺ + 2e−.
 
• At the **Cathode** (Reduction): Cu²⁺ + 2e− → Cu (pure).
 
 
 
• **Role of Sulfuric Acid**:
 
 
• Small amounts of **dilute sulfuric acid** are added to the copper sulfate solution to enhance **electrical conductivity** and prevent the precipitation of basic copper salts.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Application**:
 
 
• This method is crucial for producing copper with a **purity level** exceeding **99.9%**, which is vital for the **electrical industry** to ensure maximum conductivity in wires.

questions.question: What are the two main categories of factors that cause storage losses in agricultural products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biotic and Abiotic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Storage losses in **agricultural products** are primarily categorized into **biotic** and **abiotic** factors, which significantly impact the quantity and quality of the stored produce.
 
• **Biotic factors** comprise all living organisms that can damage the grains, including **insects**, **rodents**, **mites**, **fungi**, and **bacteria**. These organisms consume the product or contaminate it with their waste.
 
• **Abiotic factors** are non-living environmental components, with the most critical being **moisture content** and **temperature**. Inappropriate levels of these factors accelerate chemical and biological degradation.
 
• The combination of these factors leads to a series of negative outcomes such as **discoloration of produce**, substantial **weight loss**, and a significant reduction in the **germination capacity** of seeds.
 
• Proper management of these factors is essential to prevent **marketability loss**, ensuring that the food remains safe and viable for human consumption or future planting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biotic Agent Characteristics**:

 
 
• **Insects and Pests**: Species like the **pulse beetle** or **rice weevil** bore into grains, causing internal damage.
 
• **Microorganisms**: **Fungi** and **molds** thrive in high-moisture environments, often producing **toxins** that make the produce poisonous.
 
• **Rodents**: Rats and mice not only consume the grain but also damage storage structures and packaging.
 
 
 
• **Abiotic Control Measures**:
 
 
• **Drying**: Agricultural products should be dried properly in **sunlight** and then in the **shade** to reduce moisture levels to below **12%** before storage.
 
• **Temperature Control**: Maintaining a **cool environment** inhibits the metabolic rate of both the stored seeds and the pests.
 
• **Fumigation**: The use of chemical **fumigants** helps in eradicating biotic threats within the storage containers.

questions.question: An object is traveling in a straight line at a constant speed of 50 m/s. What is the displacement of the car in 10 seconds, and what type of motion does the car undergo?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**500 m and Uniform Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Displacement** is defined as the change in position of an object. For an object moving in a **straight line** at a **constant velocity**, displacement is calculated using the formula: **Displacement = Velocity × Time**.
 
• Given that the constant speed (velocity in a straight line) is **50 m/s** and the time interval is **10 seconds**, the displacement is 50 m/s × 10 s = **500 m**.
 
• **Uniform Motion** occurs when an object travels in a **straight line** and covers **equal distances** in equal intervals of time. Because the object maintains a **steady speed** of 50 m/s without any change, it is categorized as uniform motion.
 
• In this scenario, the **acceleration** of the car is **zero**, as there is no change in the magnitude or direction of the velocity vector over the 10-second period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-uniform Motion**:

 
 
• This type of motion involves an object covering **unequal distances** in equal intervals of time, indicating a **variable velocity**.
 
• It implies the presence of **acceleration** or **deceleration**, such as a vehicle moving in **congested traffic** or an object **freely falling** under gravity.
 
 
 
• **Kinematic Graphs**:
 
 
• In **Uniform Motion**, the **Distance-Time graph** is a **straight line** with a constant slope, where the slope represents the **speed**.
 
• The **Velocity-Time graph** for uniform motion is a **horizontal line** parallel to the time axis, indicating that velocity does not change with time.

questions.question: What is the importance of sexual reproduction in creating diversity within plant populations?

options.text: It combines DNA from two parents to create new variations.
It copies DNA without any changes.
This prevents any variations from occurring.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It combines DNA from two parents to create new variations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of **haploid gametes** (sperm from pollen and egg from the ovule) to form a **diploid zygote**, integrating genetic information from two distinct individuals.
 
• The process of **meiosis** is central to sexual reproduction, where **homologous chromosomes** undergo **crossing over** (recombination), exchanging genetic segments to create unique chromatids.
 
• **Independent assortment** during metaphase I of meiosis further shuffles maternal and paternal chromosomes, ensuring that each gamete has a statistically unique **genetic blueprint**.
 
• By combining diverse alleles, sexual reproduction produces **genotypic variation**, which manifests as **phenotypic diversity** within a plant population.
 
• This **genetic variability** is essential for **evolutionary adaptation**, as it allows populations to harbor traits that may provide a survival advantage against changing environmental conditions, pathogens, or predators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Asexual Reproduction Comparison:
 
 
• Unlike sexual reproduction, **asexual reproduction** (such as budding, fragmentation, or vegetative propagation) involves only one parent and produces **genetically identical clones**.
 
• It relies on **mitosis**, which specifically functions to copy DNA without changes, effectively **preventing variations** unless a random mutation occurs.
 
 
 
• DNA Copying and Mutations:
 
 
• While **DNA polymerase** occasionally makes errors during replication, biological systems have **proofreading mechanisms** to minimize these errors.
 
• Accelerating **DNA copying errors** (mutations) is generally harmful to an organism and is not a regulated mechanism for creating healthy diversity like **recombination** is.

questions.question: The mass of an object remains constant everywhere (on Earth or the Moon), whereas its weight changes due to __________________.

options.text: While the SI unit of weight is Newtons, that of mass is kilograms.
Weight depends on the local value of g, which varies depending on the location.
The amount of money depends on inertia, not weight
Weight is a scalar quantity, whereas mass is a vector quantity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weight depends on the local value of g, which varies depending on the location.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is an intrinsic property representing the quantity of **matter** in an object; it is a measure of **inertia** and remains **constant** regardless of the object's location in the universe.
 
• **Weight** is the **gravitational force** exerted on an object by a large body like a planet or a moon.
 
• The relationship between the two is defined by the formula **Weight (W) = mass (m) × acceleration due to gravity (g)**.
 
• The value of **g** (acceleration due to gravity) is determined by the **mass** and **radius** of the celestial body. On Earth, **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, while on the **Moon**, it is about **1.62 m/s²** (roughly **1/6th** of Earth's gravity).
 
• Because **weight** is directly proportional to the local **gravitational field strength**, an object's weight fluctuates as it moves between different celestial bodies or even different altitudes and latitudes on **Earth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scalar vs. Vector Quantities**:

 
 
• **Mass** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it possesses only magnitude.
 
• **Weight** is a **vector quantity** because it has both magnitude and a specific **direction** pointing toward the center of the massive body (source of gravity).
 
 
 
• **SI Units**:
 
 
• The standard **SI unit** for measuring **mass** is the **Kilogram (kg)**.
 
• Since **weight** is a force, its **SI unit** is the **Newton (N)**.
 
 
 
• **Measurement Tools**:
 
 
• **Mass** is typically measured using a **beam balance** or an **ordinary balance**.
 
• **Weight** is measured using a **spring balance**, which calculates the pull of gravity on the object.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best method to prevent iron from rusting in coastal areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galvanization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanization** is a metallurgical process where a protective **zinc coating** is applied to **iron** or **steel** components to prevent environmental **corrosion**.
 
• In **coastal areas**, the atmosphere is highly saturated with **moisture** and **sodium chloride** (salt), which acts as a powerful **electrolyte**, accelerating the **electrochemical reaction** of rusting.
 
• The process typically involves **Hot-Dip Galvanizing**, where the metal is submerged in a bath of **molten zinc** at approximately **450 degrees Celsius**, creating a series of **zinc-iron alloy layers** topped by a pure zinc outer layer.
 
• The protection provided is twofold: it offers a **physical barrier** and **cathodic protection**. Because **zinc** has a more negative **standard electrode potential** (approx −0.76V) compared to **iron** (−0.44V), it acts as a **sacrificial anode**.
 
• Even if the coating is mechanically damaged or scratched, the surrounding **zinc** will oxidize preferentially, sparing the underlying **iron** from the formation of **Fe₂O₃.xH₂O** (rust).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corrosion Mechanisms in Coastal Regions**:

 
 
• The high **relative humidity** (often above 70%) and **salinity** in marine air can increase the **corrosion rate** of unprotected iron by 10 to 100 times compared to inland desert environments.
 
• **Painting with oil-based paints** provides only a temporary barrier; **UV radiation** and salt spray in coastal zones cause paint to brittle, crack, and fail, leading to localized **pitting corrosion**.
 
• **Alloying**: Mixing iron with **Chromium** (at least 10.5%) and **Nickel** creates **Stainless Steel**, which forms a self-healing **passive film** of **chromium oxide**.
 
• **Dipping in cold water** or **periodically heating** are ineffective; in fact, heating can accelerate **oxidation** by providing the activation energy required for the reaction between iron and oxygen.
 
• **Anodizing** is another surface treatment, but it is specifically used for non-ferrous metals like **aluminum** and **magnesium** to thicken their natural **oxide layer**.

questions.question: The main reason for stars twinkling is ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmospheric refraction varying seasonally**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Stars are located at immense distances from the Earth, which makes them act as **point-sized sources** of light.
 
• When starlight enters the Earth's atmosphere, it undergoes **Atmospheric Refraction**, which is the bending of light as it passes through layers of air with different **optical densities**.
 
• The Earth's atmosphere is not uniform; it consists of multiple layers where **temperature** and **density** are constantly changing due to air currents and **seasonal variations**.
 
• Because the **Refractive Index** of these atmospheric layers is always fluctuating, the path of the starlight is continuously diverted.
 
• This causes the **apparent position** of the star to change slightly and the intensity of light reaching the eye to flicker, leading to the phenomenon known as **stellar scintillation** or twinkling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scattering of Starlight**:

 
 
• **Scattering** occurs when light rays deviate from a straight path upon hitting **dust particles** or **gas molecules** (Rayleigh scattering).
 
• While scattering is responsible for the **blue color of the sky** and the **reddish hue** of the sun during sunset, it is not the primary cause of twinkling.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Reactions**:
 
 
• Stars produce light and heat through **nuclear fusion**, where hydrogen nuclei combine to form helium under extreme **pressure** and **temperature**.
 
• This process provides the star's **intrinsic luminosity**, but the perceived flickering is an atmospheric effect, not a result of internal reactions.
 
 
 
• **Planetary Twinkling**:
 
 
• **Planets** generally do not twinkle because they are much closer to Earth and appear as **extended sources** (disks) rather than points.
 
• The **refractive variations** from different points on the planet's disk average out, resulting in a steady image.

questions.question: A compound with the molecular formula C2H4O may belong to which of the following functional groups, and what is its IUPAC name?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aldehyde, Ethanal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The molecular formula **C₂H₄O** corresponds to a compound with a **Degree of Unsaturation** (DoU) of 1. This value is derived from the formula (2C + 2 - H)/(2) , indicating the presence of either one **pi bond** (double bond) or a **ring structure**.
 
• For a two-carbon chain with one oxygen atom, the most stable structure containing a **carbonyl group** (C=O) is an **aldehyde**. The structural formula is **CH₃CHO**.
 
• In **IUPAC nomenclature**, a two-carbon aldehyde is named by taking the root name of the alkane (**ethane**) and replacing the suffix '-e' with '**-al**'. Therefore, the name is **Ethanal**.
 
• The **functional group** present is the **aldehyde group**, denoted as **-CHO**, where the carbon atom is **double-bonded** to oxygen and **single-bonded** to hydrogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ethanol**

 
 
• Formula: **C₂H₆O**.
 
• Classification: **Primary Alcohol**.
 
• Structure: **CH₃CH₂OH**. It contains only **sigma bonds** (DoU = 0) and cannot be the answer for C₂H₄O.
 
 
 
• **Ethane**
 
 
• Formula: **C₂H₆**.
 
• Classification: **Alkane** (Saturated Hydrocarbon).
 
• It contains no oxygen atoms, making it chemically inconsistent with the provided molecular formula.
 
 
 
• **Acetaldehyde**
 
 
• This is the **common name** for Ethanal.
 
• Key Uses: It is a vital intermediate in the synthesis of **acetic acid**, **ethyl acetate**, and various **synthetic resins**.
 
 
 
• **Ethenol (Vinyl Alcohol)**
 
 
• This is a **structural isomer** of Ethanal with the same formula **C₂H₄O**.
 
• However, it is highly unstable and undergoes **keto-enol tautomerization** to transform into the more stable **Ethanal** form.

questions.question: Implantation of developing embryo occurs in which part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lining of the uterus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Implantation** is defined as the process by which a developing **embryo**, specifically at the **blastocyst** stage, adheres to and embeds itself into the **inner wall** of the female reproductive organ.
 
• The specific site for this process is the **endometrium**, which is the highly vascularized and glandular **lining of the uterus** that thickens every month in preparation for potential pregnancy.
 
• This biological event typically occurs approximately **6 to 10 days** after **fertilization** has taken place in the **fallopian tube**.
 
• During implantation, the **trophoblast cells** of the blastocyst secrete **enzymes** that allow it to penetrate the uterine epithelium and sink into the **stroma**.
 
• Successful attachment triggers the production of **Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG)**, which maintains the **corpus luteum** to continue producing **progesterone**, thereby preventing the onset of menstruation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fallopian tubes**

 
 
• These are narrow tubes that link the **ovaries** to the **uterus** and serve as the primary site for **fertilization**.
 
• If an embryo implants here instead of the uterus, it results in an **ectopic pregnancy**, which is a medical emergency.
 
 
 
• **Ovary**
 
 
• The primary female reproductive organ responsible for **oogenesis** (production of eggs) and the secretion of **estrogen**.
 
• It does not host the embryo; its role ends with **ovulation**, the release of the mature **oocyte** into the peritoneal cavity.
 
 
 
• **Cervix**
 
 
• The lower, narrow portion of the **uterus** that opens into the **vagina**.
 
• Its main functions include controlling the passage of **sperm** into the uterus and protecting the fetus during **gestation** by remaining tightly closed.

questions.question: When several rays parallel to the principal axis fall on a concave mirror, how do the reflected rays behave?

options.text: They spread out and appear as if they are emerging from behind the mirror.
They reflect back along the same path.
All of them meet at a single point on the principal axis.
They travel parallel to the principal axis after reflection.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of them meet at a single point on the principal axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a type of spherical mirror where the reflecting surface is curved inwards, towards the **Center of Curvature**.
 
• When incident light rays travel **parallel to the principal axis** and strike the concave mirror, they undergo **reflection** based on the geometry of the sphere.
 
• According to the **laws of reflection**, the reflected rays converge because the normal at the point of incidence (the radius) slants towards the principal axis.
 
• This convergence causes all parallel rays to intersect at a specific fixed point on the principal axis, which is defined as the **Principal Focus (F)**.
 
• Since the light rays actually meet at this point in front of the mirror, the **Principal Focus** of a concave mirror is a **real point**.
 
• The distance between the **Pole (P)** of the mirror and the **Principal Focus (F)** is known as the **focal length (f)**, which is related to the **Radius of Curvature (R)** by the formula **f = R / 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diverging Behavior**:

 
 
• In contrast to concave mirrors, **convex mirrors** cause parallel rays to spread out after reflection.
 
• These rays appear to originate from a **virtual focus** located behind the mirror, which is why convex mirrors are called **diverging mirrors**.
 
 
 
• **Reflection through Center of Curvature**:
 
 
• If a ray of light passes through the **Center of Curvature (C)**, it strikes the mirror surface **perpendicularly** (along the normal).
 
• In this case, the angle of incidence is 0 degrees, causing the ray to reflect back along its **original path**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications**:
 
 
• Concave mirrors are utilized in **solar furnaces** to concentrate sunlight at a point to produce high heat.
 
• They are also used as **reflectors** in **torches** and **vehicle headlights** to produce powerful parallel beams when the light source is placed at the focus.

questions.question: Six resistors each of 3 Ω are connected in parallel in a loop. What will be their effective resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In an electrical circuit, when resistors are connected in a **parallel combination**, the **reciprocal** of the **equivalent resistance** (Rₚ) is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
• The standard formula for calculating the **effective resistance** for resistors in parallel is 1/Rₚ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + ... + 1/Rₙ.
 
• When all resistors in the parallel arrangement have the same resistance value, the formula simplifies to **Rₚ = R / n**, where **R** is the resistance of a single resistor and **n** is the total number of resistors.
 
• In this problem, the resistance of each component is **3 Ω** and the total number of resistors is **6**.
 
• Applying the simplified formula: **Rₚ = 3 / 6**.
 
• Performing the division gives a result of **0.5 Ω**, representing the total resistance offered by the loop to the current flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voltage and Current in Parallel Circuits**:

 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the **Potential Difference (Voltage)** across every resistor remains **constant** and is equal to the source voltage.
 
• The **total current** entering the parallel network splits among the branches inversely proportional to their resistance, following **Kirchhoff's Current Law**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Series Circuits**:
 
 
• In a **series circuit**, the equivalent resistance is the sum of all individual values: Rₛ = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ.
 
• If these six 3 Ω resistors were connected in series, the effective resistance would be 3 × 6 = **18 Ω**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Significance**:
 
 
• **Domestic Wiring**: Households use parallel circuits so that every appliance receives the same **220V** (or 110V depending on the region) and can be operated independently.
 
• If one resistor in a parallel loop fails (becomes an open circuit), the remaining branches continue to function normally, unlike in a series circuit.

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes a food web from a food chain?

options.text: The food chain always has decomposers; it does not have a food web.
A food web transfers total energy; a food chain loses energy.
A food web allows for a bidirectional flow of energy; a food chain is unidirectional.
A food web illustrates multiple trophic levels, whereas a food chain illustrates a single level.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A food web illustrates multiple trophic levels, whereas a food chain illustrates a single level.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **food chain** represents a linear sequence of organisms where nutrients and **energy** are transferred, showing a **single pathway** of consumption.
 
• In this linear model, each organism is assigned to a **single trophic level**, simplifying the complex interactions found in nature for easier study of **biomagnification**.
 
• A **food web** is a complex network formed by several interconnected **food chains**, which more accurately depicts **ecosystem** relationships.
 
• While a chain shows a single connection, a **food web** illustrates **multiple trophic levels** simultaneously, as many organisms eat more than one type of prey and can occupy various positions.
 
• Energy flow in both models is **unidirectional**, meaning it moves from **producers** to higher-order **consumers** and does not cycle back, following the laws of **thermodynamics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ecological Concepts and Components**:

 
 
• **Decomposers**: Organisms like **fungi** and **bacteria** that break down dead organic matter; they are essential to both **food chains** and **food webs** to recycle nutrients.
 
• **Lindeman's 10% Law**: Formulated by **Raymond Lindeman** in **1942**, it states that only about **10%** of the energy is transferred to the next **trophic level**, while **90%** is lost as **respiration** or heat.
 
• **Trophic Levels**: Usually categorized into **Primary Producers** (plants), **Primary Consumers** (herbivores), **Secondary Consumers** (carnivores), and **Apex Predators**.
 
• **Ecosystem Stability**: Complex **food webs** provide greater **stability** than chains because they offer alternative food sources if one species population declines.

questions.question: What is the main difference between isobars and isotopes?

options.text: While isobars have the same atomic number, isotopes have different atomic numbers.
While isotopes are atoms of the same element, isobars belong to different elements.
Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers.
While isobars have the same number of electrons, isotopes do not.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isobars** are defined as atoms of different chemical elements that possess the same **mass number** but have different **atomic numbers**. The mass number is the sum of **protons** and **neutrons** in the nucleus.
 
• Because **isobars** have different atomic numbers, they represent different **chemical elements** and occupy different positions in the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• **Isotopes** are variants of the same chemical element. They have the same **atomic number** (number of protons) but a different **mass number** because they contain a different number of **neutrons**.
 
• The **atomic number** determines the identity of an element and its **chemical properties**; therefore, isotopes of an element behave similarly in chemical reactions, while isobars exhibit entirely different chemical behaviors.
 
• The **physical properties** of isobars, such as density and boiling point, are typically different because they belong to different elements, despite having similar **atomic masses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of Isobars**:

 
 
• **Argon** (atomic number 18) and **Calcium** (atomic number 20) both can have a mass number of 40. They are **isobars**.
 
• **Iron** and **Nickel** can also form isobaric pairs, such as those with a mass number of 58.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Isotopes**:
 
 
• **Hydrogen** has three primary isotopes: **Protium** (0 neutrons), **Deuterium** (1 neutron), and **Tritium** (2 neutrons). All have 1 proton.
 
• **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14** are isotopes used in biological studies and **radiocarbon dating**.
 
 
 
• **Isotones**:
 
 
• These are atoms of different elements that have the same number of **neutrons** but different atomic numbers and mass numbers. For example, **Carbon-14** (8 neutrons) and **Oxygen-16** (8 neutrons) are isotones.

questions.question: A current-carrying wire is placed between magnetic poles. A maximum force acts on it when it is ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Perpendicular to the magnetic field**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The mechanical force exerted on a current-carrying conductor placed within an external **magnetic field** is a result of the **Lorentz Force** acting on the moving electrons.
 
• The magnitude of this force is defined by the mathematical expression **F = B I L sin θ**, where **F** is the force in **Newtons**, **B** is the **magnetic flux density** (Tesla), **I** is the **current** (Amperes), **L** is the **length** of the conductor (meters), and **θ** is the angle between the conductor and the magnetic field lines.
 
• The force is directly proportional to the **sine** of the angle **θ**; therefore, the force varies from zero to a maximum value based on the **orientation** of the wire.
 
• When the wire is **Perpendicular** to the magnetic field, the angle **θ** is **90°**. Since **sin 90° = 1** (the maximum possible value for the sine function), the force reaches its maximum possible magnitude, calculated as **F = B I L**.
 
• This **maximum force** principle is essential for generating the highest possible **torque** in **electric motors**, where the armature windings are designed to cut field lines at right angles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallel and Antiparallel Alignment**:

 
 
• If the conductor is placed **Parallel** (0°) or **Antiparallel** (180°) to the magnetic field, **sin θ** becomes **0**.
 
• In this orientation, the magnetic field exerts **no force** on the current-carrying wire, meaning the wire remains stationary regardless of the current strength.
 
 
 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**:
 
 
• This rule provides the **orthogonal direction** of the force. When the **forefinger** (field), **middle finger** (current), and **thumb** (force) are held mutually **perpendicular**, they indicate the relationship between the three vectors.
 
• The rule confirms that the force is always **perpendicular** to the plane containing both the **current** and the **magnetic field**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Flux Density (B)**:
 
 
• Commonly referred to as **magnetic field strength**, it is measured in **Tesla (T)** or **Webers per square meter (Wb/m²)**.
 
• The force increases linearly with the strength of the **permanent magnets** or **electromagnets** used to create the field.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding Rutherford's atomic model is/are correct?

Statement 1: An atom possesses a positively charged, dense nucleus at its center.

Statement 2: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular orbits without losing energy.

Statement 3: Most of the space inside an atom is empty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rutherford's **Alpha-particle scattering experiment** revealed that a very small fraction of particles were deflected by large angles, indicating that the positive charge and most of the mass are concentrated in a centrally located, extremely small, and dense region called the **nucleus**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• In Rutherford's model, he proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus in **circular orbits**. However, he could not explain why these moving charges would not radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus; the postulate that electrons revolve in specific orbits **without losing energy** was a cornerstone of the **Bohr Atomic Model**, not Rutherford's. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Observations showed that the vast majority (over 99%) of alpha particles passed through the **gold foil** without any deviation, which led to the conclusion that **most of the space** inside an atom is **empty**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rutherford's Atomic Model (Planetary Model)**:

 
 
• Proposed in **1911** following the landmark gold foil experiment conducted by **Geiger and Marsden**.
 
• Introduced the concept of the **atomic nucleus**, which is approximately 10⁵ times smaller than the total diameter of the atom.
 
• Calculated that the **radius of the nucleus** is about 10−¹⁵ meters, while the **radius of the atom** is about 10−¹⁰ meters.
 
 
 
• **Limitations and Evolution**:
 
 
• According to **Maxwell's electromagnetic theory**, any charged particle in circular motion (acceleration) must lose energy via **electromagnetic radiation**.
 
• The instability problem of the Rutherford model was later addressed by **Niels Bohr** in 1913, who introduced **stationary energy levels** or **shells**.
 
• The model eventually paved the way for the discovery of the **proton** and later the **neutron** by **James Chadwick**.

questions.question: An object travels 16 m in 4 s, and then another 16 m in 2 s. What is the average speed of the object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5.33 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Average Speed** of an object describes the total path length covered relative to the total duration of the trip.
 
• The **total distance** traveled by the object is the sum of both segments of its journey: 16 m + 16 m = **32 meters**.
 
• The **total time taken** to complete the entire journey is the sum of the time intervals: 4 s + 2 s = **6 seconds**.
 
• The formula for average speed is calculated as: Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time).
 
• Substituting the known values into the equation: Average Speed = 32 m ÷ 6 s = **5.333... m/s**.
 
• Rounding the result to two decimal places provides the final answer of **5.33 m/s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Characteristics of Speed**:

 
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: Speed is categorized as a **scalar quantity** because it only provides magnitude and does not specify a direction.
 
• **Standard Units**: The **SI unit** for speed is meters per second (**m/s**). Other common units include kilometers per hour (km/h) and miles per hour (mph).
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion**: In this problem, the object covers 16 m in 4 s (speed of 4 m/s) and then 16 m in 2 s (speed of 8 m/s); this variation in speed confirms the object is in **non-uniform motion**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula**: The physics dimensions for speed are expressed as [M⁰L¹T−¹], indicating it is proportional to length and inversely proportional to time.
 
• **Speedometer and Odometer**: While a **speedometer** records the **instantaneous speed** of a vehicle, the **odometer** records the total distance traveled.

questions.question:
Choose a word to complete the analogy.

Columnar epithelial tissue: absorption:: Cuboidal epithelial tissue: ____________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mechanical Support**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The analogy compares different types of **epithelial tissues** with their primary physiological roles in the human body.
 
• **Columnar epithelial tissue** is composed of tall, pillar-like cells typically found in the inner lining of the **intestine** and **stomach**. Its structure facilitates the movement of substances across the epithelial barrier, aiding in **absorption** and **secretion**.
 
• **Cuboidal epithelial tissue** consists of cube-shaped cells with central, spherical nuclei. It is primarily found in the **lining of kidney tubules** and the **ducts of salivary glands**.
 
• The structural integrity of cuboidal cells provides **mechanical support** to the secretory and excretory organs, ensuring they maintain their shape and function under physiological pressure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ciliated Columnar Epithelium**:

 
 
• These cells possess hair-like projections called **cilia** on their outer surface.
 
• Their primary function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction, such as **expelling phlegm** and trapped dust from the **respiratory tract**.
 
 
 
• **Stratified Squamous Epithelium**:
 
 
• This tissue is arranged in many layers to **prevent wear and tear** and accidental injuries.
 
• It is predominantly found in the **skin**, where its multi-layered structure acts as a protective barrier.
 
 
 
• **Simple Squamous Epithelium**:
 
 
• This is a single layer of extremely thin, flat cells that **form a delicate lining**.
 
• It is found in locations where the transportation of substances occurs through a selectively permeable surface, such as **lung alveoli** and **blood capillaries**.

questions.question: Which of the following products is formed when ethene (C2H4) reacts with hydrogen (H2) in the presence of a nickel catalyst?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethane (C2H6)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical reaction between **ethene** (C₂H₄) and **hydrogen** (H₂) is a classic example of an **addition reaction**, specifically known as **catalytic hydrogenation**.
 
• In this process, the **carbon-carbon double bond** (π-bond) in ethene is broken, allowing two hydrogen atoms to be added to the carbon atoms.
 
• The reaction requires a catalyst such as **Nickel (Ni)**, **Palladium (Pd)**, or **Platinum (Pt)** to lower the activation energy; when **Nickel** is used, the reaction typically requires a temperature between **150°C and 300°C**.
 
• The product formed is **Ethane** (C₂H₆), which is a saturated hydrocarbon belonging to the **alkane** family.
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is: **C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturated vs. Unsaturated Hydrocarbons**:

 
 
• **Ethene** is an **unsaturated hydrocarbon** because it contains a double bond, making it more reactive.
 
• **Ethane** is a **saturated hydrocarbon** containing only single bonds, resulting in lower chemical reactivity.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Nickel Catalyst**:
 
 
• **Nickel** provides a solid surface for **adsorption**, where hydrogen molecules dissociate into atoms, facilitating their addition to the ethene molecule.
 
• This specific industrial application is used in the **hydrogenation of vegetable oils** to produce solid fats like **margarine** or **vanaspati ghee**.
 
 
 
• **Analysis of Other Options**:
 
 
• **Ethyne (C₂H₂)**: An **alkyne** with a triple bond; its formation would require the removal of hydrogen (**dehydrogenation**), not addition.
 
• **Propene (C₃H₆)** and **Propane (C₃H₈)**: These are **three-carbon** chains; they cannot be formed from **ethene** (two carbons) via simple hydrogenation as there is no source of extra carbon.

questions.question: Lysosomes are also known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Suicidal bags of the cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the **Golgi apparatus**.
 
• They are filled with **hydrolytic enzymes** such as **lipases**, **proteases**, and **carbohydrases**, which are optimally active at an **acidic pH**.
 
• The primary role of these organelles is the **intracellular digestion** of macromolecules, damaged cellular parts, and foreign invaders like **bacteria** or **viruses**.
 
• If the cell gets damaged or experiences a metabolic disturbance, the **lysosomal membrane** may rupture, causing the released **digestive enzymes** to consume the cell’s own contents.
 
• This process of self-destruction, known as **autolysis**, is why lysosomes are famously called the **suicidal bags** of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy powerhouses**:

 
 
• This refers to **Mitochondria**, which are responsible for producing **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)** through the process of **aerobic respiration**.
 
 
 
• **Control centers**:
 
 
• This identifies the **Nucleus**, which contains the **genetic material (DNA)** and coordinates essential activities such as **growth**, **metabolism**, and **reproduction**.
 
 
 
• **Protein factories**:
 
 
• This term describes **Ribosomes**, the sites where **amino acids** are assembled into proteins based on instructions from **mRNA**.
 
 
 
• **Discovery**:
 
 
• Lysosomes were discovered by the Belgian scientist **Christian de Duve** in the mid-**1950s**, a discovery that contributed to his **Nobel Prize** in Physiology or Medicine.

questions.question: Which of the following describes a key function of lysosomal enzymes?

options.text: Breaking down proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates
Creating new proteins for the cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Breaking down proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles containing a variety of **hydrolytic enzymes** (acid hydrolases) that are capable of digesting all types of biological polymers.
 
• The primary function of these enzymes is **intracellular digestion**, where they break down macromolecules such as **proteins**, **lipids**, **polysaccharides**, and **nucleic acids** into their basic building blocks.
 
• These enzymes function most efficiently in an **acidic environment**, typically maintaining a **pH of about 4.5 to 5.0** within the lysosomal lumen, which is regulated by **proton pumps** in the membrane.
 
• Lysosomes are often referred to as the **suicide bags** of the cell because if the cell is damaged beyond repair, the lysosomes can burst and release enzymes to digest the entire cell, a process known as **autolysis**.
 
• Beyond digestion of external materials, they are essential for **autophagy**, which involves the degradation of the cell's own obsolete or damaged **organelles** to recycle nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Storing genetic material**:

 
 
• This is the function of the **Nucleus**, which contains the cell's **DNA** organized into **chromosomes**.
 
 
 
• **Transporting molecules across the membrane**:
 
 
• This role is performed by the **Plasma Membrane** (cell membrane) through mechanisms like **active transport**, **facilitated diffusion**, and **ion channels**.
 
 
 
• **Creating new proteins for the cell**:
 
 
• This is the primary function of **Ribosomes**, which can be found in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum**.
 
 
 
• **Discovery**:
 
 
• Lysosomes were discovered by the Belgian cytologist **Christian de Duve** in **1955**, for which he later received a **Nobel Prize**.

questions.question: Metals like iron and zinc, which are in the middle of the activity series, are generally summarized (concluded) as follows:

options.text: A heating process involving no reducing agent of any kind.
Reduction of their oxides with carbon or carbon monoxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduction of their oxides with carbon or carbon monoxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metals placed in the **middle of the reactivity series**, such as **Iron (Fe)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Lead (Pb)**, and **Copper (Cu)**, are considered moderately reactive and are often found as **sulfide** or **carbonate** ores.
 
• Since extracting a metal from its **oxide** is chemically more efficient, these ores are first converted into oxides through **Roasting** (heating sulfide ores in excess air) or **Calcination** (heating carbonate ores in limited air).
 
• The **metal oxides** are then **reduced** to their respective metallic states using a suitable **reducing agent** like **carbon (coke)** or **carbon monoxide**.
 
• This chemical process, known as **Smelting**, involves the carbon reacting with the oxygen in the metal oxide to form carbon dioxide or monoxide, leaving behind the metal: **ZnO + C → Zn + CO**.
 
• For **Iron**, the reduction occurs in a **blast furnace** where **carbon monoxide (CO)** acts as the primary reducing agent to convert **Haematite (Fe₂O₃)** into molten iron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis of molten salts**

 
 
• This method is utilized for **highly reactive metals** (e.g., **Sodium**, **Aluminium**, **Calcium**) located at the top of the activity series.
 
• These metals have a very high **affinity for oxygen**, making it impossible to reduce them using carbon.
 
 
 
• **Heating without a reducing agent (Self-reduction)**
 
 
• Metals at the **bottom of the activity series** (e.g., **Mercury**, **Silver**) are so unreactive that their oxides can be reduced to metal by **heat alone**.
 
• For example, **Cinnabar (HgS)** is converted to **Mercuric Oxide (HgO)** and then reduced to **Mercury (Hg)** simply by continued heating.
 
 
 
• **Displacement from aqueous solution**
 
 
• Used for extracting less reactive metals by treating their **salt solutions** with a **more reactive metal** (e.g., using **Iron** to displace **Copper** from **Copper Sulfate**).

questions.question: A bus moves from one end A to the other end B of a straight 1000 m road in 100 s and then turns around and moves 500 m back to point C in another 100 s. What will be the average velocity (in m/s) and the type of motion of the bus in going from point A to point C?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.5 m/s and Non-Uniform Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Displacement** is defined as the shortest straight-line distance between the **initial position** (Point A) and the **final position** (Point C). The bus travels 1000 m from A to B and then returns 500 m towards A to reach C. Therefore, the net displacement is 1000 − 500 = **500 meters**.
 
• The **total time taken** for the entire journey from A to C is the sum of the time taken from A to B and from B to C. This equals 100 s + 100 s = **200 seconds**.
 
• **Average Velocity** is calculated by dividing the **total displacement** by the **total time taken**. Using the values derived, Average Velocity = 500 / 200 = **2.5 m/s**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion** occurs when an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time or when its **direction of motion** changes. In this scenario, the bus moves at 10 m/s (1000/100) initially and then at 5 m/s (500/100) in the opposite direction. Since the **velocity** (magnitude and direction) is not constant, the motion is classified as **Non-Uniform**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uniform Motion**:

 
 
• An object is said to be in **uniform motion** if it travels in a straight line and covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**.
 
• The **acceleration** in uniform motion is always **zero** because the velocity remains constant throughout the duration of the movement.
 
 
 
• **Average Speed**:
 
 
• Unlike velocity, **average speed** depends on the **total distance** traveled rather than displacement.
 
• For this journey, the total distance is 1000 + 500 = 1500 m. The average speed would be 1500 / 200 = **7.5 m/s**.
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** requiring both magnitude and direction, whereas **speed** is a **scalar quantity**.

questions.question:
Examine the two statements given below and select the correct option.

Statement A: Nervous tissue is responsible for the rapid transmission of electrical impulses within the body.

Statement B: Nervous tissue primarily provides structural and mechanical support to organs.

options.text: A is not correct, but B is correct.
Two statements, A and B, are not correct.
A is correct, but B is not correct.
Two statements, A and B, are correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is correct, but B is not correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nervous tissue** is highly specialized to receive **stimuli** and transmit **electrical impulses** (action potentials) throughout the body to coordinate various functions. Hence, statement A is correct.
 
• The **neurons**, which are the functional units of the nervous system, possess the property of **excitability** and **conductivity**, allowing for the rapid relay of information across **synapses**. Hence, statement A is correct.
 
• **Connective tissue**, rather than nervous tissue, is the primary tissue responsible for providing **structural and mechanical support**, protection, and binding of different organs. Hence, statement B is incorrect.
 
• While **nervous tissue** facilitates communication and control, it lacks the dense **extracellular matrix** (like collagen fibers found in connective tissue) required to serve as a structural framework. Hence, statement B is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of Nervous Tissue**:

 
 
• **Neurons**: Specialized cells consisting of a **cell body (cyton)**, **dendrites** (receive signals), and a long **axon** (transmits signals).
 
• **Neuroglia**: Also called **glial cells**, these provide metabolic support, insulation (via **myelin sheaths**), and protection to neurons but do not conduct impulses.
 
 
 
• **Other Primary Tissue Types**:
 
 
• **Epithelial Tissue**: Functions in protection, secretion, and absorption across **membranes** and **glandular structures**.
 
• **Muscular Tissue**: Composed of elongated cells that contract to produce **locomotion** and movement within internal organs.
 
• **Connective Tissue**: Includes specialized forms like **bone**, **cartilage**, and **adipose tissue**, which provide the actual mechanical strength and support to the human anatomy.
